subject: Life Skills
title: Your Right to a Refund
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Your Right to a Refund.

hook.text: Many stores say 'no refunds' but consumer protection laws in most states override that policy.

buildup.text: If a product is defective, you are legally entitled to a repair, replacement, or refund in most places.

discovery.text: Implied warranties exist even without a written guarantee. Products must work for their intended purpose.

twist.text: 'As is' labels can legally waive implied warranties in many states. Read before buying used goods.

climax.text: Keep receipts, know your state's consumer protection laws, and escalate to your attorney general if needed.

punchline.text: Store policy doesn't override the law.

quiz.question: What is an implied warranty?
options: A written guarantee provided by the manufacturer
A legal expectation that products work for their purpose
An extended warranty you purchase separately
